evidence.excerpt:
test - If a parser wants to read the value of the field "returned" by multiple
  *   child parsers, make sure to read the field into a local variable after
  *   each child parser is complete to make sure the value you want from an
  *   earlier child isn't stomped over by a later child
  *
  *   In general, for a parser to "return" a value in a mutable field, it is
  *   sufficient to simply set the value of that field before returning. It
  *   is the parent-parser's responsibility to make sure it reads out the value
  *   of the field to a local variable before running another child parser that
  *   will over-write the mutable field
evidence.interpretation: The implementation documents child results being returned through one mutable run. Source-derived invariant: snapshot the earlier child's fields before evaluating another child. This is deliberate allocation control, not accidental effectful application state.
evidence.timestamp_basis: Commit committer timestamp for the pinned snapshot; not a claim that these lines were introduced then.

claims.rule: Inference from implementation and documented examples: when extracting a Fastparse higher-order combinator, defer executable child parser expressions and preserve each child's saved value, index and diagnostic fields before executing the next child on the shared ParsingRun.
claims.applicability: Fastparse 2-era by-name wrappers and compiler-specific macro expansion; a Scala 3 implementation must be checked for inline/by-name staging rather than mechanically copying Scala 2 syntax. Preserve the direct synchronous parser model; no Cats Effect, ZIO or Ox conversion is supported by this history.
claims.counterexample: Ordinary immutable Parsed results can be stored and passed by value. A macro's surface P parameter may be staged by the compiler rather than behaving as an ordinary eager method; inspect the expansion before flagging it.

claims.rule: When changing cuts in a reusable whitespace/comment parser, trace its enclosing repetition and alternate branch, then add a separate issue-named minimal regression asserting the semantic result and consumed index rather than altering an existing success fixture.
claims.applicability: The separate-regression request is explicit reviewer guidance in PR 256. Tracing the declarationList/comment control flow and checking stream-buffer safety are source-derived inferences. Cuts determine both backtracking and when old input can become inaccessible.
claims.counterexample: Do not remove every cut to make one input pass: after a uniquely identifying grammar prefix a cut may intentionally reject malformed input and bound retention. Nor does a successful prefix parse prove whole-input acceptance without checking its final index or End.

claims.rule: Inference: before consolidating repetition implementations, enumerate compiler-specific overloads and which parameters are statically specialized, then preserve minimum/maximum/exactly, separator, whitespace, cut and failure-message behavior across the remaining paths. Evaluate runtime and generated-code size separately.
claims.applicability: The Scala 2 source explains specialization versus code-bloat and named-argument tradeoffs; the 2024 Scala 3 implementation uses a general macro with static-value inspection. The hygienic-name observation is a reviewer comment specific to Scala 3 quotes, not a benchmark or a universal macro rule. Supplemental PR 323 supplies only an in-window reviewer question and author-reported compiler difference; its open proposal/current diff is not adopted implementation evidence.
claims.counterexample: Shared source is not automatically slower and duplicated source is not automatically required: the later Scala 3 macro shares an implementation while retaining specialization. PR 274's author-reported slowdown is not an independently reproduced measurement or a universal rejection threshold.

claims.rule: When reviewing an implicit or given used as a combinator hook on the shared run, reject function-typed values (P[_] => P[Unit]) that Scala 2 can also apply as implicit conversions; use a dedicated trait or SAM type. Add a minimal regression that ascribes the conversion-triggering type (for example `def f[T: P]: P[Unit] = Fail.!`) and asserts Parsed.Failure.
claims.applicability: PR 272 (merged 2023-03-02, Scala 2.11-2.13 and Scala 3 cells). The root cause is the author's statement; the dedicated trait and test are source. The change was binary incompatible and lihaoyi timed it for the 3.0.0 major version; route the ABI decision to library-contract guidance.
claims.counterexample: A function-typed parameter that is explicit (not implicit) cannot be inserted as a view. A user grammar that already uses the Whitespace trait does not need this review.

claims.rule: For a Fastparse Scala 2-to-3 macro port, preserve Scala 2 coverage and exercise consumer grammars, not just the core suite. Separate host-compiler source changes from recognized-language changes, and re-probe .rep/.repX call syntax before imposing a migration rewrite.
claims.applicability: This boundary is explicit in the 2022 discussion and was revisited during the 2023 port. The 2024 split Scala compiler test adapter demonstrates patch-version-sensitive compiler internals; historical acceptance reports are not a build result from this research run.
claims.counterexample: Adding Scala 3 grammar syntax to ScalaParse is separate work and must not be made a prerequisite for compiling Fastparse on Scala 3. A defect limited to a Scala 2.13 compiler-internal test hook does not justify modifying the shared grammar.
